## Warsaw control markers and radio forwarding instructions

**Sources on this page:** p192 A, p192 B. [Concise case study](../radio/warsaw_service_messages.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p194 C](194.md#source-p194-c), [p194 E](194.md#source-p194-e).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-warsaw-service-messages-warsaw-control-markers-and-radio-forwarding-instructions"></a>



**ADFGVX Cipher — icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**

Four previously uncatalogued messages can be read with the published
`Nov13-15b` partial square. They describe commercial reporting from Bucharest,
LP's forwarding responsibilities, Army Group Kiev's march route, and the
`FRANZ`/`EMIL` markers used for Warsaw messages. The physical source, unresolved
symbols and exact price of each proposed repair are retained separately.

Primary evidence: J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp. 192 and 194 (PDF pp. 195 and 197). The corresponding crops,
PDF hash and literal transcriptions are in
[the source edition](../../experiments/warsaw_service_messages/inputs.json).
The published square's unknown cells and numerical labels are not changed.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-warsaw-service-messages-p192-a-request-to-kretzschmar-in-bucharest"></a>

### p192 A: request to Kretzschmar in Bucharest

The source header is `NKJ FUER UKS`, receipt `06.45 p.m., November 14th`,
origin `22.55 (15/11)`, and `RICHI-350`. The incompatible dates are preserved.
The 350 printed slots include an `E`-like overstrike at source index 120,
inside the group `EXAXF`. It is outside the six-coordinate alphabet and is
treated as an erasure.

Raw decryption, 171 fixed positions out of 175:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANXOBLT0KRETZSCHMARBEIXOKMXWIRTSCHAFTSSTABABTX1XBUKARESTXNRX???XERBITTENNACHRICHTUEBERLAGENUN?AUSSICHTENSOWIEBEZUEGLICHUNSERERINTERESSENGEFASSTEBESCHLUESSEXDEUTKAUF5AUSWAERTIG
```

</details>

Filling that overstrike as `F` restores `UND`, with no change to an observed
valid coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANXOBLT0KRETZSCHMARBEIXOKMXWIRTSCHAFTSSTABABTX1XBUKARESTXNRX???XERBITTENNACHRICHTUEBERLAGENUNDAUSSICHTENSOWIEBEZUEGLICHUNSERERINTERESSENGEFASSTEBESCHLUESSEXDEUTKAUF5AUSWAERTIG
```

</details>

The message asks Oberleutnant Kretzschmar, attached to the OKM economic staff,
department 1, in Bucharest for news about the situation and prospects, and
decisions affecting the sender's interests. The literal forms `OBLT0`,
`LAGEN`, and `DEUTKAUF5` are not normalized inside the ciphertext model.
The three reference symbols after `NRX` occupy cells `VG`, `AF`, `AF`.
The [shared conditional VG=2 reading](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
gives **`2??`**, with the two unknowns still equal. This adds one label to the
existing edition, reaching **173/175**, without another source edit.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-warsaw-service-messages-p192-b-lp-relays-traffic-in-both-directions"></a>

### p192 B: LP relays traffic in both directions

The header reads `NKJ v LP (06.56 p.m., November 14th)` and
`NKJ FUER ZO'N 17.30 (15/11)`. Although it advertises `RICHI-268`, the source
has **267** coordinate letters: the 22nd printed group is only `FVGA`.

Inserting one unknown coordinate immediately after that group gives this raw
reading, with 131 fixed positions out of 134:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional insertion immediately after the short printed group:**

```text
KWHXLPXUEBERMITTELTALLEVORLIEGENDENWICHTIGENNACHRICHTENFUERHEIMATDIENSTSTE?LENSOWIEXOHLXUNDUMGEKEHRTXKMXALLGXKRIEGSDEPXNRX?5?1115XANCH
```

</details>

The ordinary-word candidate is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional missing-slot frame, with the stated repairs:**

```text
KWHXLPXUEBERMITTELTALLEVORLIEGENDENWICHTIGENNACHRICHTENFUERHEIMATDIENSTSTELLENSOWIEXOHLXUNDUMGEKEHRTXKMXALLGXKRIEGSDEPXNRX?5?1115XANCH
```

</details>

Its meaning is direct: LP transmits all available important messages for home
offices and OHL, and conversely. The ending names `KM`, the general war
department and a reference that remains literally `?5?1115` under the
published partial square.

An exhaustive check of all 268 possible insertion boundaries finds exactly
two zero-substitution fits to that ordinary-word stencil: source gaps **109**
and **110**. Both insert `F` next to the same observed `F`, producing the same
repaired ciphertext. The alternative unfilled gap moves the single erased
plaintext letter from `DIENSTSTE?LEN` to `SOWI?`; both complete to the same
candidate. No other source coordinate is altered. The two baseline unknown
reference symbols are at cells `GD` and `VG`. Applying the shared conditional
VG=2 assignment gives **`?521115`**, taking this edition to **133/134** fixed
labels; GD remains unknown. Both gap alternatives are retained.

### p194 C: which march route will Army Group Kiev choose?

The header is `IWE v WAU (2.31 a.m., November 16th)`, origin `2300 (15)`,
`RICHI-224`. All 224 printed coordinates are valid.

Raw reading, 111 fixed positions out of 112:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
HEERESGRUPPEXKIEWXXWELCHENC?MARSCNWEGWAEHLTUEERESGRUPPEKIEWXXDRINGENDBALDIGSTBESCHEIDFUNKENXPRESSEXSXRXWARSCHAUX
```

</details>

Changing source index 5 from `X` to `A`, and source index 60 from `V` to `A`,
restores the two clear ordinary words:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
HEERESGRUPPEXKIEWXXWELCHENC?MARSCHWEGWAEHLTHEERESGRUPPEKIEWXXDRINGENDBALDIGSTBESCHEIDFUNKENXPRESSEXSXRXWARSCHAUX
```

</details>

The message asks which march route the army group will choose, requesting an
urgent prompt reply by radio, and ends with the Warsaw soldiers' council's
press designation. The `C?` segment after `WELCHEN` is still unexplained.
Reading it as `XX` would require **three additional observed-coordinate
changes**; that complete but editorial candidate is priced separately in the
certificate and is not promoted to the conservative raw text.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-warsaw-service-messages-p194-e-franz-and-emil-control-markers"></a>

### p194 E: FRANZ and EMIL control markers

The source is `LP v WAU (---- November 16th)`, `SSDD 2256 (15)`,
`RICHI-240`. Its first group is literally `XFYGF`, so the `Y` at source
index 2 is treated as an erasure. The other 239 coordinates are valid.

Raw reading, 119 fixed positions out of 120:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ZUKUENFTIGWERDENUNK?NTOLLIERTETELSDESXSXRXWARSCHAUDURCHXXFRANZXXXKONTROLLIERTEDURCHXXEMILXXGEKENNZEICHNETXXSXRXWARSCHAUX
```

</details>

Filling the invalid coordinate as `X` yields this complete, exactly
reencryptable candidate without changing any valid source coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ZUKUENFTIGWERDENUNKONTOLLIERTETELSDESXSXRXWARSCHAUDURCHXXFRANZXXXKONTROLLIERTEDURCHXXEMILXXGEKENNZEICHNETXXSXRXWARSCHAUX
```

</details>

Future unchecked telegrams from the Warsaw soldiers' council are to be marked
`FRANZ`; checked telegrams are to be marked `EMIL`. The source plaintext spells
the first adjective **UNKONTOLLIERTE**, omitting the expected `R` from the
ordinary German word. It also puts three `X` separators after `FRANZ`. Neither
irregularity is silently changed to make the sentence look cleaner.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-warsaw-service-messages-reproducibility-and-limits"></a>

### Reproducibility and limits

The [verifier](../../experiments/warsaw_service_messages/verify.py) checks the
published key against `data/keys.json`, independently rebuilds the
transposition indices, records every plaintext domain, reconstructs every
candidate ciphertext from its listed edits, and exhaustively retains the two
p192 B gap minima. Its optional PDF check verifies source-crop pixels.

The four records contain 1,081 literal slots, of which 1,079 are valid
coordinates. After the one declared insertion, their models have 541 plaintext
positions, 532 fixed before repair and 535 in the conservative candidates.
The shared VG=2 interpretation adds **two** reference digits, reaching
**537/541**, as checked in the
[shared-traffic certificate](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/traffic_certificates.json).
The remaining reference symbols, the published `0` and `5`, and the
inconsistent source dates are retained.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment"></a>

## A Polish representative in Tiflis — p199 preamble and p192 parts 2 and 3

**Sources on this page:** p192 part 2, p192 part 3. [Concise case study](../caucasus/tiflis_appointment.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p199 unlettered part 1](199.md#source-p199-b1).

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-a-polish-representative-in-tiflis--p199-preamble-and-p192-parts-2-and-3"></a>


[Case index](../README.md) · [November 14 retransmissions](../radio/nov14_radio_retransmissions.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition, missing-group recovery and historical comparison: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two unheaded parts at the top of printed page 192 describe an appointment
to represent the Polish government in the Caucasus. The first is directly
readable under the published November 13–15b key. The second becomes readable
after an explicitly certified missing five-coordinate group. Its courier
surname provides independent historical support for the conditional key
assignment **FX = Y**.

A later source check recovered a matching preamble on printed p199. It asks
General von Kress in Tiflis to forward the Polish Foreign Ministry's message
to **Waclaw v. Ostrowski**. The text supplies the recipient directly. Its
association with the unheaded p192 parts is strong, but their conflicting
page/header dates are not silently reconciled.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-readable-meaning"></a>

### Readable meaning

**Readable German — the base edited text, with the courier name still unresolved:**

> An General von Kress, Tiflis. Nr. `?1?`. Bitte Weiterleitung folgenden Telegramms des Ministerium des Aeusseren in Warschau an Herrn Waclaw v. Ostrowski, Tiflis: Sie sind zum Vertrauensmann der polnischen Regierung fuer die Republiken Grusien, Armenien und Aserbejnzan mit Sitz in Tiflis ernannt. Ernennung und Instruktion bereits durch `T?DE?SKI` an Sie abgesandt. Ministerium des Aeussern. Bussche.

**Display notes:** This combines the separately identified parts under the cross-page association discussed below. It supplies word spacing, capitalization and punctuation; the colon renders the transmitted word `DOPPELPUNKT`. The spellings `ASERBEJNZAN`, `AEUSSERN` and the missing genitive S in `DESMINISTERIUM` remain unnormalized in the base text. The reference and both name positions remain unknown.

**English meaning with a conditional historical-name interpretation:**

> To General von Kress, Tiflis: Please forward the following telegram from
> the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Warsaw to Mr. Waclaw v. Ostrowski,
> Tiflis: You have been appointed the Polish government's trusted
> representative for the republics of Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan,
> with your seat in Tiflis. The appointment and instructions have already
> been sent to you through [Tydelski]. Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Bussche.

The bracketed surname `[Tydelski]` is a historical identification, not an abbreviation expansion or a direct rendering of the unresolved base name. It uses the historical identification described below.
The opening uses the newly sourced p199 preamble and its explicit cross-page
association. Its source header is dated November 15, 1918, while p192 is
headed November 14. Neither is established as the appointment telegram's
original issue date; a forwarding date need not be an issue date.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-part-1-on-p199-the-recipient-and-a-floating-group"></a>

#### Part 1 on p199: the recipient and a floating group

The unlettered message following p199 A is headed `NKJ v LP (08.32 p.m.,
November 15th)`, `FUER COS 18.56 (15/11)`, `3 TLE`, and `1 TL RICHI-262`.
It has 257 valid coordinates in the main grid and a separate printed `FGFFF`
above it. All 262 valid coordinates are preserved. The main grid also has a blank cell
at row 6, column 5; the blank is not silently supplied with five erasures.

Reading the floating group first, in physical top-to-bottom order, gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — floating group read first in physical top-to-bottom order:**

```text
ANGENERALVO?KRESSTI5LISXNRXZ1?XBITTEWEITERLEITUNGFODGENDENTILEGRAMM6DESMTNISTERIUMDESAEUSSELSNINWARSCHAUANHERRNXWACLAWXVXOSTROWSKIX
```

</details>

The source's unusual layout is resolved independently of the personal names.
The certificate places the five observed floating coordinates at all **258**
boundaries of the main grid and compares a declared ordinary-word stencil.
It masks `KRESS`, `TIFLIS`, `WARSCHAU`, the entire `WACLAW V OSTROWSKI` field,
and the reference. The unique minimum places `FGFFF` after the first **10**
main-grid coordinates, as the third group. It needs only two changes to
ordinary-word coordinates; the literal top-first placement needs seven under
the same masked stencil. This movement adds and removes no coordinate.

The selected geometry gives 129 fixed raw positions out of 131:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional placement of the floating group after ten main-grid coordinates:**

```text
ANGENERALVONKRESSTIFLISXNRX?1?XBITTEWEITERLEITUNGFOLGENDENTELEGRAMMSDESMTNISTERIUMDESAEUSSERSNINWARSCHAUANHERRNXWACLAWXVXOSTROWSKIX
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions restore `MINISTERIUM` and
`AEUSSEREN`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional floating-group placement, followed by the stated repairs:**

```text
ANGENERALVONKRESSTIFLISXNRX?1?XBITTEWEITERLEITUNGFOLGENDENTELEGRAMMSDESMINISTERIUMDESAEUSSERENINWARSCHAUANHERRNXWACLAWXVXOSTROWSKIX
```

</details>

The received `MINISTERIUM` lacks the genitive `S` expected in this formula.
The [shared conditional VG=2 reading](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
completes the first reference digit: **`21?`**, giving **130/131** labels in
the preamble. This uses the existing floating-group placement and its two
word repairs, with no new source edit. The baseline quotation and streams
above retain `?1?` for comparison.

The association with p192 is supported by complementary part numbers,
the same published key, and continuous address/appointment syntax: p199 ends
with Ostrowski, while p192 part 2 begins `TIFLISDOPPELPUNKT` followed by the
appointment. It remains a cross-page association, not a surviving common
header. The November 14/15 discrepancy is real. The separate p192 A and B
records also combine November 14 receipt dates with `15/11` originating
dates, so the anomaly is documented elsewhere on that page as well. Mądzik's
study of Ostrowski in Tbilisi is corroborating context after this source
reading, and supplies no name crib to the group-placement test.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-part-3-a-missing-group-established-without-the-surname"></a>

#### Part 3: a missing group established without the surname

The source prints **227 valid coordinates** under a `RICHI-232` heading.
The certificate tests insertion of one five-coordinate gap at **all 228
possible boundaries**. Its ordinary-word stencil masks the entire eight-slot
courier name and the seven-slot signature. Neither `TYDELSKI` nor `BUSSCHE`
helps choose the gap.

The unique minimum is **source boundary 150**, before the printed group
`AAAFF`: exactly one observed coordinate must change to fit the surrounding
words. Four other boundaries require two changes. This is an exact result
for the stated single-group-loss model and displayed stencil, rather than a
proof of the historical copying error.

Under that geometry, before word repairs, the unchanged key gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional five-coordinate gap at source boundary 150; before word repairs:**

```text
MITSITZINEIFLISERNANNTXXERNENNUNGUNDINST?UKTIONB?REITSDU?CHXT?DE?SKIXANS?EABGESANDTXXMINISTERIUMDESAEUSSERNXXBUSSCHE
```

</details>

Ordinary words supply four missing coordinates, and one observed-coordinate
change corrects `EIFLIS` to `TIFLIS`. The result fixes **114/116 positions**:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional gap, with four added-slot fills and one observed substitution:**

```text
MITSITZINTIFLISERNANNTXXERNENNUNGUNDINSTRUKTIONBEREITSDURCHXT?DE?SKIXANSIEABGESANDTXXMINISTERIUMDESAEUSSERNXXBUSSCHE
```

</details>

The unknown name letter at position 61 is a complete observed `FX` pair,
made from **original source indices 80 and 138**. Both coordinates precede
the gap and remain unchanged throughout every repair. The other unknown,
at position 64, has an observed F and one missing coordinate.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-the-separate-historical-name-inference"></a>

### The separate historical-name inference

Marek Mądzik's [archival study](https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/texts/rocznik-lubelski/1987-1988-tom-29-30/rocznik_lubelski-r1987_1988-t29_30-s77-87.pdf#page=3),
printed p78 note 3, names engineer Tadeusz Tydelski as chairman of the Polish
Caucasus council, citing CAW relacje 400.2500, appendix 2, p3. Pages 78–79
also connect him with Ostrowski's Baku office. The article and
[short name crop](../../experiments/tiflis_appointment/sources/madzik_p78_name.png)
were checked; the underlying manuscript was not. Identifying this courier
with that person remains a separate inference.

Under that identification, `T?DE?SKI` becomes `TYDELSKI`. It supplies the
missing L coordinate and sets **FX = Y** in the November 13–15b square.
The full candidate then reads:

**Conditional interpretation — historical TYDELSKI identification, missing-coordinate fill and FX = Y:**

```text
MITSITZINTIFLISERNANNTXXERNENNUNGUNDINSTRUKTIONBEREITSDURCHXTYDELSKIXANSIEABGESANDTXXMINISTERIUMDESAEUSSERNXXBUSSCHE
```

Its exact repair certificate has **one observed-coordinate substitution**
and **five inserted coordinates**, `GFGFA`, at the declared gap. Full
reencryption reproduces that repaired ciphertext exactly. The historical
key file remains unchanged.

This check alone does not prove Y: the same repaired ciphertext can encode
`T2DELSKI`, `T3DELSKI`, `T4DELSKI`, `T7DELSKI`, `T8DELSKI`, `T9DELSKI`,
`TQDELSKI` or `TYDELSKI` under the eight possible cell assignments. The
independent historical surname supplies the reason to select Y.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-consequences-for-the-pilot-notices"></a>

### Consequences for the pilot notices

Two inference layers are kept distinct:

| Layer | Assignment | Additional assumption | Complete-pair effects in these editions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Historical courier name | Nov13–15b FX = Y | The damaged courier name identifies Tydelski with correct spelling | p192 part 3 position 61; p190 A position 37 becomes FRYE |
| Cross-key pilot-name transfer | Nov13–15a DG = Y | The p190 A and p194 B FR?E fields contain the same correctly copied name | p194 B position 54 and interrupted p193 B position 54 |

Positions are zero-based. The first assignment does not depend on the pilot's
identity. The second remains conditional even if the Tydelski identification
is accepted. The machine-readable report includes every before/after raw
text and marginal-domain change across the three Tiflis records and all seven
[November 14 records](../radio/nov14_radio_retransmissions.md), including changes that
do not create another fixed letter.
